tasks.short: Prepare vocational practice materials and adapted instructions, give additional instruction in vocational skills, and record each student's practice progress.

steps.what: Special education teacher prepares adapted instructions for vocational areas

loop.input: The original work instruction for the vocational task and the target reading level.
loop.output: The instruction rewritten in simpler language with short numbered steps.
loop.check: Code checks every safety warning and every step of the original appears in the rewrite; the teacher reads, adds pictures and approves.
loop.stop: One rewrite per instruction; if a check fails twice, the teacher rewrites it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Simplifying technical text for students with learning disabilities needs rewording, not a template.

steps.what: Special education teacher provides additional instruction in vocational areas
Special education teacher records each student's practice progress on paper lists

tasks.design: A bounded step rewrites work instructions for vocational tasks in simpler language with short steps; code checks every safety warning and step is kept, and the teacher reads and adds pictures. Practice progress goes into a skills checklist in the pupil record system ({OTHER}) on a tablet. Instructing students stays with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions were rewritten by hand and progress kept on paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson tools rewrite text at another level.
tasks.still_hard: Each student needs a different level and pace.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a student the same step for the tenth time with patience.
tasks.altitude: The teacher checks rewritten instructions instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether adapted instructions help at the workplace.

evidence.claim: LessonUp's lesson editor rewrites text at another level, summarises and translates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the vocational task to the practice record; internships are outside.
Input contract: work instructions from the vocational department or employers; fallback is rewriting by hand.
No student data go into the rewrite step.
research_questions: Do students work more independently with adapted instructions?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher reads and approves rewrites.

incremental.description: Special education teacher adds pictures to rewritten instructions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few written instructions; high: many new vocational tasks each term.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the agenda and documents, attend staff meetings, write proposals for committees, and find documents and decisions from earlier meetings.

steps.what: Special education teacher reads the agenda and documents before meetings
Special education teacher attends staff meetings and serves on committees
Special education teacher writes proposals for committees
Special education teacher searches e-mail for documents and decisions from earlier meetings

tasks.design: Agendas, documents and a running decisions list for each committee sit in one shared folder ({DOCS}), so earlier decisions are found without searching e-mail. Committee proposals use a short template. Meetings and committee work stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents and decisions were spread over e-mails.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared folders with decision lists are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Decision lists are only as good as the secretary keeps them.
tasks.human_edge: Speaking up for students with support needs when the school sets priorities.

evidence.claim: Shared folders with decision lists and proposal templates are standard office tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the meeting agenda to the committee proposal; carrying out decisions is outside.
Input contract: the committee secretary keeps the decisions list; fallback is e-mail.
research_questions: Do fewer questions about earlier decisions come up in meetings?

incremental.description: Special education teacher files committee documents in the shared folder.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one committee; high: several committees with long histories.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search for courses, conferences and workshops, choose one with the team leader, register, attend to maintain professional competence, log hours and certificates, and share what was learned.

steps.what: Special education teacher searches for courses, educational conferences and teacher training workshops
Special education teacher chooses a course with the team leader
Special education teacher registers for the course
Special education teacher attends professional meetings and workshops to maintain professional competence
Special education teacher logs hours and certificates in the professional portfolio
Special education teacher shares what was learned with colleagues

tasks.design: The school's learning system ({LMS}) lists courses matched to the teacher's development goals, and certificates from course providers land in the portfolio without retyping hours. Choosing with the team leader, registering, attending and sharing stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Courses were found by browsing many sites and hours logged by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems list courses and store certificates.
tasks.still_hard: Courses on special needs are scarce and fill fast.
tasks.human_edge: Bringing back one idea the team will really use.

evidence.claim: Learning systems can list courses by goal and store certificates with hours.

assumptions: Boundary: from development goals to learning shared; the course content is outside.
Input contract: course catalogue in the learning system; fallback is browsing and logging by hand.
Attending and sharing do not change.
Course fees are approved as today.
research_questions: Is the portfolio complete at the yearly review?

incremental.description: Special education teacher checks certificates arrived in the portfolio.

approvals.approved_version: The course as chosen with the team leader in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one course a year; high: several short workshops.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the class project or field trip, collect parent consent and medical information, arrange guest speakers, check the plan with the team leader, book transport and venue, supervise the activity, and guide students in learning from it.

steps.what: Special education teacher plans class projects and field trips
Special education teacher collects parent consent forms and medical information on paper
Special education teacher arranges visits by guest speakers by e-mail
Special education teacher checks the final plan with the team leader
Special education teacher books transport and the venue
Special education teacher supervises the trip, project or guest visit
Special education teacher guides students in learning from the activity

tasks.design: A trip checklist template in the document space ({DOCS}) lists venue, transport, staffing ratio, medication and emergency contacts, so plans are not built from scratch. Parents give consent and medical details in the parent app, which the teacher sees as a list instead of collecting paper slips. Once the team leader has checked the plan, the teacher books transport and venue. Supervising and guiding students stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were built from scratch and consent slips collected on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Parent apps collect consent; checklist templates are easy to share.
tasks.still_hard: Students with disabilities need extra staff and accessible venues.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a student calm in a new place with crowds and noise.

reach.learn: Whether medical information is at hand on the trip.

evidence.claim: Parent apps can collect consent and contact details; checklist templates can be shared.
Medical details of students are health data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the activity idea to students reflected; trip budgets are outside.
Input contract: consent forms set by the school; fallback is paper slips.
Parents fill consent in the app in about the time a paper slip took; no added parent time.
Supervising and guiding do not change.
research_questions: Are all consents in before the trip more often?

incremental.description: Special education teacher reminds parents who have not responded.

approvals.approved_version: The plan as checked with the team leader in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one short trip; high: many trips and projects in a year.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The special education teacher keeps instructing, attending meetings and courses, and supervising activities; rewritten instructions, e-mail searches and paper slips shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with more time for practice and trips.
